player.name: Wren Ashdown
player.concept: a quick-witted half-elf ranger with a longbow, a dry sense of humour and a soft spot for underdogs

canon: Wren reached the undercroft unseen, took Hester's weight, and lowered her safely onto the walkway.
Snikkit noticed Wren's rescue; Gubbin's snoring stopped and the curtain stirred.
Hester told Wren that the goblins had been waiting at the ford and went straight for her satchel.
notes: Keep Hester safely on the walkway and let Wren choose whether to flee, negotiate, or face the waking warren; don’t force a fight from the curtain stirring alone. As Hester engages, land her urgency about reaching Caerwyn before the Assembly and her reluctance to travel barefoot and alone.

repairs.assessment: Wren is enjoying careful, practical play and has successfully rescued Hester without a roll-over into the race. The scene is on track, with Snikkit noticing and Gubbin stirring creating immediate pressure.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The burnt mill’s roof has fallen in, leaving a gap in the floor. From above, you see the black mill-race roaring through its stone channel, tallow lamps guttering along the walkways. Six goblins lean on spears and slings, while a narrow one astride the hoist beam rests a knife against the rope. Below him, a woman in a grain sack hangs over the water, turning slowly.

“—and under any reasonable interpretation of the terms,” she says, “this is not how one obtains a royal document.” The goblin gives the rope a little twitch. “Chief wants king-paper by moonrise, paper-lady. Moon’s nearly up.” At the far end, something large snores behind a moth-eaten curtain. No one below has looked up. What do you do?

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I stay low at the lip of the gap, out of the lamplight, and study the hoist before doing anything: where the rope runs, where it is tied off, how far she would drop, and how fast that water is moving below her. I nock an arrow but do not draw.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
From the shadowed lip, you can see the arrangement clearly. The rope passes through a sack-hoist pulley fixed to the beam, then runs to Snikkit’s hand. He has tied off the free end beside him; his knife rests where one quick cut would drop Hester into the race. She hangs a yard above the water, just beside the wall’s plank walkway.

The current is fast and black, dragging scraps of mill straw towards a low culvert. The goblins below are grumbling softly about Gubbin’s appetite. Snikkit hushes them with a look, still listening to Hester explain the legal distinction between a demand and a contract. Your arrow is ready; no one has noticed you. What do you do?

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: If that rope is cut she drowns in a sack, so the first job is to be close enough to catch her. I sling the bow across my back, work along the edge of the gap to the wall side, and lower myself down the charred joists onto the plank walkway beside her, slowly, staying in the shadow of the wall.

transcript.speaker: dice
transcript.text: Stealth check to reach the undercroft without being seen: 8 + 5 = 13 vs DC 13: success

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Your weight settles on the wall-side plank with barely a creak. The race roars beneath you, swallowing the small sounds; the guttering lamps throw the walkway’s other edge into shadow. You’re close enough to see the knife’s nicked edge against the rope, and close enough to catch Hester if you can get her down onto the planks.

Snikkit leans towards her, purring, “A mutual arrangement, paper-lady. You write the king-paper, nobody gets wet.”

“I see,” Hester says. “And if I decline?”

“Then we discuss the alternatives.”

His fingers tighten on the rope. He hasn’t seen you. What do you do?

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I brace one boot against the wall, reach out and take a firm grip on the rope just above the neck of the sack, so that if he cuts it I have her weight and not the river. I keep my voice under the noise of the water. "Keep talking, madam. Do not look at me. I have hold of you."

transcript.speaker: dice
transcript.text: Acrobatics check to seize the courier before the goblins notice: 16 + 4 = 20 vs DC 12: success

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Your braced boot holds. When Snikkit’s hand shifts on the rope, you catch it above the sack and take Hester’s weight before he can cut. You lower her onto the plank walkway, sack scraping the stone; the current claws at the loose hem but doesn’t get her.

Hester keeps her eyes on Snikkit, as you asked. “I am continuing to discuss the alternatives,” she says, with admirable crispness and a tremor she has not quite managed to file away.

Then Snikkit looks down. His knife hangs still. Across the cellar, the snoring behind the curtain stops.

Hester turns to you, breathing hard. “That was no chance raid. They were waiting at the ford—and went straight for my satchel.” Behind her, the curtain stirs. What do you do?

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I cut the cord at the neck of the sack with my belt knife so she can get her arms out, and keep myself between her and the goblins. "Questions later. Stay behind me and stay on the planks." Then I unsling the bow, nock, and hold it half-drawn on Snikkit, and speak up so they can all hear me over the water. "Nobody move. The lady is leaving with me. Nobody needs to be hurt tonight, and I would prefer it that way."

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The cord parts, and Hester pulls her arms free of the sack. She stays on the planks behind you, as ordered, one hand clamped over the satchel.

Snikkit’s eyes flick from your drawn bow to the rope you’ve spoiled. “Now, tall friend,” he says softly, “let’s not make an unfortunate arrangement more unfortunate.”

The curtain parts. A huge goblin in a copper pot peers out, bone sceptre raised. “What is this noise? We is king!”

Hester’s voice is crisp, though she’s shivering. “I must reach the Saltmere delegation in Caerwyn before the Assembly opens. And, if it is not too much to ask, I would rather not walk there barefoot and alone.”

whispers.note: Once Wren has a moment to respond, make clear you need to reach the Saltmere delegation before the Assembly and would rather not walk the road barefoot and alone.
You’ve lost the rope as leverage and Wren has shown they can act decisively; try to keep control of the moment without provoking a fight you may not win.
You have heard the disturbance and are waking; protect your authority by demanding to know what has happened before committing to violence.
